The present application under Section 528 of the BNSS has been filed seeking the grant of interim bail to the Petitioner.

6. Learned counsel for the Petitioner has submitted the following reasons for the grant of interim protection to the Petitioner herein:-
(i) The Petitioner was granted bail vide Order dated 27.03.2025 passed by the learned Additional Sessions Judge-03, South East, Saket Courts, Delhi ["ASJ"] and has remained on bail upto the Order dated 30.05.2025 passed by the learned ASJ.

sentences.text: Throughout this period, he has never misused the liberty granted to him.
(ii) While the co-accused in the aforementioned FIR has not joined the investigation, the Petitioner is being unfairly penalised despite having joined the investigation.
(iii) The Petitioner has been cooperating with the investigation and has appeared before the concerned authorities at least 12 times on various dates.

(iv) The present proceedings are a result of a personal vendetta against the Petitioner and have been initiated subsequent to the Petitioner's retirement from the company, which he served faithfully for over 25 years.
(v) The Petitioner is a 60-year-old man currently This is a digitally signed order.

(vi) The Petitioner does not pose any flight risk, and the same is evident from the fact that, post registration of FIR and before the issuance of Look Out Circular against the Petitioner, he had travelled to the United Arab Emirates for 7 days on 28.11.2024 and duly returned to India.
7. Issue notice.

Learned APP for the State and the learned counsel for Respondent No.
2/Complainant appear on advance notice and oppose the grant of any kind of interim relief to the Petitioner.
8. Be that as it may, this Court considers it necessary to have on record the replies of the Respondents in order to take any decision on the interim relief as sought by the Petitioner.
